p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines the difference between a *fact* and a *decision*, why recording decisions is load-bearing in a human-AI team, the four fields every record carries, *where* records live (at the governing spec anchor, not in an ADR silo), *when* to write one, and the two section patterns for larger documents.

p.a-fact-is-recovered-with-one-grep: Any reader — human or agent — recovers it from the code in a second with one grep.

p.BLAKE3-WITH-ITS-REASON-IS-A-DECISION: "We hash with blake3 because SHA-256 drags in an OpenSSL dependency, and we need minimal binary size for edge servers on weak hardware" is a **decision**.

p.no-grep-recovers-a-decision: No grep recovers it: the constraint lives outside the code, and the code is byte-identical either way.

p.ASYMMETRY-IS-ABSOLUTE: The asymmetry is absolute: **a fact is recoverable from the code in a second; a decision cannot be recovered at all.**

p.reasoning-is-gone-once-it-leaves-working: Once reasoning leaves working memory — the human's after two months, the agent's at session end — it is gone unless written down.

p.DECISION-FORM-IS-WORTH-TEN-FACT-FORMS: The decision form is worth ten of the fact form.

why.title: Why this is load-bearing in a human-AI team

p.tribal-knowledge-in-a-pure-human-team: In a pure-human team, unrecorded reasoning survives as tribal knowledge: "Why this library?" — "Vasya tried five alternatives three months ago; only this one worked with our glibc."

p.EVERY-SESSION-IS-A-NEW-DEVELOPER-WITH-ZE: Every session is a brilliant new developer with zero project memory: knowledge that is not in a file the agent can read does not exist for it.

item.FAILURE-RE-DERIVATION: **Re-derivation.** The code shows the value, not the constraint. The agent sees `TIMEOUT = 600`, finds no reason, concludes the number is arbitrary, and proposes 300 s "for performance" — the 15 % of VPN users who needed the 600 s are invisible in the code.

item.FAILURE-RE-LITIGATION: **Re-litigation.** Every unrecorded decision is re-opened by every future reader, at an hour of re-analysis per re-open — with no guarantee of the same answer, because the original data is gone.

p.RECORD-IS-IMMUNITY-FROM-RE-LITIGATION: A recorded decision is **immunity from re-litigation**: the next proposal to "optimise" the timeout is answered by the record in one read, not an hour of archaeology.

p.TRIGGER-FIELD-KEEPS-THE-IMMUNITY-HONEST: The trigger field keeps the immunity honest — without it the decision hardens into a sacred cow ([`revisit-triggers.md` §sacred-cows](revisit-triggers.md#sacred-cows)).

p.EVERY-RECORD-CARRIES-EXACTLY-FOUR-FIELDS: Every record carries exactly four fields:

td.fact: The chosen value or approach. One line.
The observation that forced the choice — concrete, measured, cited. Name the data: log path, sample size, benchmark, incident, upstream constraint.
One line per alternative, each carrying the reason it lost. A loser without a reason invites the evaluation to be re-run.
A measurable trigger: metric + threshold + where it is observed. "Later" is not a trigger.

p.why-three-of-the-four-fields-exist: Three of the four fields exist so the argument is *never re-had*: the why answers "is this arbitrary?", the rejections "did you consider X?", the trigger "is it time to reconsider?".

p.RECORDS-LIVE-AT-THE-GOVERNING-ANCHOR: **At the spec anchor that governs the value.**

p.timeout-record-sits-under-the-verificati: The timeout record lives in the spec section that defines verification timing — under the very heading a reader lands on when asking "why 600?".

p.departure-from-classic-adr-lead: This deliberately departs from classic ADR practice:

td.fact: The record sits inside the governing spec section

td.ROW-ADR-IMMUTABLE: Immutable, append-only; changes chain via "superseded by ADR-0042"

td.fact: The section is edited in place; a dated changelog line notes the change; git holds the history

td.ROW-ADR-MUST-BE-SOUGHT: The reader must know the ADR exists and go find it

td.fact: The record rides along with every read of the section

p.agent-loads-context-by-anchor: An agent loads context by anchor: when it reads the section governing the value, a co-located record arrives for free, at the exact moment of temptation to "fix" the value.

p.a-record-in-a-silo-is-never-looked-up: A record in a silo requires the agent to know to look — and it will not, because nothing at the anchor points at `adr/0007`.

p.SILOS-PRESERVE-TECHNICALLY-AND-LOSE-PRAC: Silos preserve reasoning technically and lose it practically.

item.CONSEQUENCE-NO-ADR-DIRECTORY: **No `adr/` directory.** The spec tree is the only home.

item.CONSEQUENCE-SPEC-SECTION-IS-THE-RECORD: **The spec section IS the record.** No second artefact to sync.

item.CONSEQUENCE-EVOLUTION-IS-AN-EDIT: **Evolution is an edit.** Rewrite the record in place, add a dated changelog line; the old text is one `git log -p` away. Procedure: [`revisit-triggers.md` §when-fired](revisit-triggers.md#when-fired).

item.CONSEQUENCE-RECORDS-ARE-CITABLE: **Records are citable.** Give every record's heading an explicit anchor — `spec://<project>/<doc>#<anchor>` or any stable path-plus-anchor form — so comments and commits can point at it.

p.WRITE-A-RECORD-FOR-ANY-REOPENABLE-CHOICE: Write a record for any choice a future reader could plausibly re-open:

td.fact: blake3 over SHA-256; one HTTP client over another
timeouts, retry counts, buffer sizes, thresholds
wire format, schema, identity scheme, directory layout
a road not taken that someone will propose again
a review gate, a commit convention, a naming law

p.DO-NOT-RECORD-WHAT-HAS-NO-PLAUSIBLE-ALTE: Do **not** write records for facts with no plausible alternative, or for implementation details the next refactor invalidates — those rot faster than they pay back.

p.THE-COMPETENT-NEWCOMER-TEST: The test: *would a competent newcomer, reading the code cold, plausibly propose changing this?*

p.WRITE-IN-THE-SESSION-THAT-DECIDES: The moment of writing is the moment of deciding — same session, before it ends.

p.backfilled-reasoning-is-fiction: Reasoning unwritten at session end does not survive it; a record backfilled a week later is fiction with confidence.

rejected-alternatives.title: The rejected-alternatives section

p.bigger-documents-outgrow-a-single-record: Bigger documents — design proposals, subsystem specs — accumulate more rejected options than fit in one record.

p.CLOSE-BIG-DOCUMENTS-WITH-A-REJECTED-OPTI: Close the document with a section where **every rejected option gets one line with its reason**:

rejected-alternatives.fence:
## Rejected alternatives {#rejected}
- **A one-time hardening pass instead of a recurring process** — rejected: a one-shot pass decays the day after it lands. - **Rely on the per-commit gate alone** — rejected: the gate is a regression detector, blind by construction to uncovered code. - **Fully automate the audit now** — deferred, not rejected: value is breadth plus judgment; automation grows category by category.

p.why-the-line-with-reason-format: The line-with-reason format is the entire value: a bare list of losers invites the evaluation to be re-run; a reasoned list answers the future proposal before it is made.

p.MARK-HONEST-DEFERRALS-AS-DEFERRED-NOT-RE: Mark honest deferrals *deferred, not rejected* — a deferral has a built-in revisit.

invariants-restatement.title: The invariants restatement

p.FOUNDATIONAL-DOCUMENTS-CLOSE-WITH-INVARI: Foundational documents — the ones pinning decisions every other document assumes — close with an **Invariants** section: the most load-bearing decisions as one-liners, each pointing at its record.

p.why-the-restatement-earns-its-place: The restatement is a concession to attention: a hurried reader — or an agent deep into a long session — reads the invariants even when reading nothing else; each line points back at the full reasoning.

re-derive.title: Re-derive for your project

p.COPY-THE-TASK-NOT-THE-EXAMPLES: Do not copy this protocol's examples verbatim — copy the *task*, and let the agent re-derive the records the project actually needs:

re-derive.fence: Read this flow's documents (your project installed them — typically `vibedeps/flow-decision-records/<version>/spec/flows/decision-records/`, check `vibe.lock`) in full, then adapt the practice to this project: 1. Inventory where design decisions currently live here (spec tree, ADR directory, wiki exports, README sections, commit messages). 2. List the ten decisions a newcomer would most plausibly re-open — library picks, constants with consequences, protocol shapes, rejected approaches — with the file and anchor governing each. 3. For each, draft the four-field record (Decision / Why / Considered and rejected / When to revisit) at that governing anchor. Where you cannot source a why, write TODO(owner) — never invent data. 4. Propose revisit triggers only from signals this project actually observes: CI timings, monitoring, benchmarks, dependency audits. 5. Show me the drafts as diffs. Apply nothing until I approve.

item.SUM-RECORD-DECISIONS-NOT-FACTS: A fact is recoverable from the code in a second; a decision cannot be recovered at all. Record decisions.

item.SUM-FOUR-FIELDS-ALWAYS: Four fields, always: Decision / Why (measured, cited) / Considered and rejected (one line each, with reasons) / When to revisit (a measurable trigger).

item.SUM-RECORDS-LIVE-AT-THE-ANCHOR: Records live at the governing spec anchor. No ADR silo; the section is the record; git is the history.

item.SUM-RECORD-IN-THE-SAME-SESSION: Record in the same session the decision is made.

item.SUM-CLOSING-SECTIONS-BY-DOCUMENT-SIZE: Bigger docs close with rejected alternatives; foundational docs with an invariants restatement.

item.SUM-IMMUNITY-AND-ITS-TRIGGER: A recorded decision is immunity from re-litigation; the trigger keeps it from becoming dogma.
